overall: The AG found that a planning board member's email to a quorum of the board expressing an opinion on a pending application was an unlawful deliberation, but the board as a whole was not in violation.

allegations.summary: A planning board member emailed the other members, a quorum, expressing a critical opinion on a pending gas station application and stating an intent to vote against it.
allegations.key_passage: Expression of an opinion on matters within the body's jurisdiction to a quorum of a public body is a deliberation, even if no other public body member responds.

allegations.summary: The complaint alleged the Board as a whole communicated outside a posted meeting about the project before the hearing, through the member's email.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find only an individual violation of the Open Meeting Law by Mr. Rangel, and not a violation by the Board as a whole.

remedy: Review the Open Meeting Law Guide available at the Attorney General's Open Government website, www.mass.gov/ago/openmeeting.
Within thirty (30) days of the date of the letter, certify in writing to the Attorney General's office that he has reviewed the determination and the Guide.
remedy_passage: We find that Mr. Rangel violated the Open Meeting Law and direct him to review the Open Meeting Law Guide available at the Attorney General's Open Government website, www.mass.gov/ago/openmeeting.
